learner.title: Your learning journey starts here
learner.subtitle: Courses, records, support, and your next step—one clear topic at a time.

slides.title: Your first five minutes
points: Confirm your name and assigned program
Review the next required action
Keep your own sign-in secure
slides.narration: Start with the name and program on your dashboard. Confirm that both belong to you. Read the next required action before opening a new task. A dashboard card summarizes a saved record; open the card to see its details. Never share your password or work from another person’s account. If the wrong program, organization, or student appears, stop and report it to support.

slides.title: Documents: upload, review, correction
points: Upload only the requested item
Submitted does not mean approved
Read correction notes before replacing a file
slides.narration: Open Documents and Records. Select the requirement, choose a readable file, and submit it through the protected upload form. Check the saved status after uploading. Pending review means staff must review the evidence; it does not mean you should upload it again. If an item is rejected, read the correction note and replace only that item. The generic learner intake confirmation upload has been retired. Do not send identity or tax documents through ordinary messages.

slides.title: Find your course and resume learning
points: Open My Courses
Follow the assigned lesson order
Complete activities and real quizzes
slides.narration: Open My Courses and select your assigned program. Use Continue to return to unfinished work. Review the pictures, narration, reading, and examples before answering the knowledge checks. Complete required activities yourself, then confirm that your progress saved. A partner course may open another provider’s website and require its assigned login. Follow the access instructions on your account. Report a missing link, unexpected purchase request, or incorrect course instead of buying a second course.

slides.title: Plan your study week
points: Check the syllabus and calendar
Complete lessons, practice, and quizzes
Contact staff before missing a deadline
slides.narration: Read the syllabus for your own program’s sequence, pace, assessments, and completion requirements. Self-paced study gives you flexibility within the assigned schedule; it does not remove deadlines. Set a weekly study routine, take notes, and practice before taking a quiz. Review feedback and use the allowed retry or correction process. Check the calendar for confirmed appointments and join the meeting link at the scheduled time. Ask your assigned instructor about a schedule conflict before the deadline.

slides.title: Track attendance and learning evidence
points: Use the correct attendance tool
Check saved hours and feedback
Request corrections with actual dates
slides.narration: When your program requires attendance or a study clock, open Attendance and follow the instructions for that activity. Online study time and supervised work time are different records. Record only time you actually completed and do not run overlapping clocks. At the end of a session, confirm the entry saved. If an entry is missing or incorrect, report the date, actual start and finish times, and what you were doing. Staff must review corrections before hours are credited.

slides.title: Messages, meetings, and getting help
points: Check Inbox and announcements
Explain the exact blocked step
Keep sensitive records in protected uploads
slides.narration: Use your dashboard messages or support workspace for training questions. Explain your program, page or lesson, what you selected, and the error you saw. A screenshot can help, but hide passwords, payment details, and private identity numbers. Check Sent after sending a message and Inbox for replies. PARIS can help explain navigation; staff must resolve approvals, account access, and record corrections. Ask for accessibility support or an alternative format when you need it.

slides.title: Finish training and prepare for work
points: Complete every assigned requirement
Submit earned credentials for review
Build your résumé and review career tools
slides.narration: A finished video is one part of learning. Program completion can also require quizzes, assignments, attendance, supervised competencies, and verified credential evidence. Check your completion checklist with your program contact. Certification testing and a course completion certificate can be separate steps. Upload credentials you earn outside Elevate for verification. Start your résumé while you train and add only skills and credentials you can support. Use the career tools to prepare for applications and next steps.

slides.title: Inter-office email: contact your Elevate team
points: Open your mailbox and choose Compose.
Use your assigned staff contact and a clear subject.
Check Inbox for replies and keep the same conversation.
slides.narration: Use inter-office email inside your dashboard as your regular way to communicate with Elevate staff. Open the mailbox, choose Compose, and select or enter the staff address provided in your program instructions. Include your full name, program, the page or lesson involved, and what help you need. Send the message, check Sent, and return to Inbox for replies. Reply in the same conversation so staff can follow the history. If your mailbox is unavailable or your contact is missing, use Learner Support to report it. Do not send passwords or Social Security numbers.

slides.title: Community: learn with your peers
points: Browse groups for your program or study interests.
Join a group, ask a question, and reply respectfully.
Use inter-office email for private questions to staff.
slides.narration: Open Community to connect with other learners and find study groups. Choose Browse groups, read the group description, and join a group relevant to your program. Introduce yourself, ask a learning question, or share a useful study resource. Read replies and respond respectfully. Community conversations can be visible to other members, so keep personal documents, financial information, and account details out of posts. Questions about your enrollment, document review, attendance corrections, or individual support belong in inter-office email to your assigned staff contact.

slides.title: Career services: explore your job feed
points: Start career services while you are training.
Review job requirements, location, and closing dates.
Open the listing to follow the employer’s application steps.
slides.narration: Career Services is available while you train and as you prepare for your next step after training. Open your personalized career feed and review the opportunities shown. Check the job duties, location, requirements, application instructions, and closing date before applying. A suggested opportunity is not a job offer or a guarantee that you meet every requirement. If no matches appear, you can still open the résumé builder and placement center. Contact your program team through inter-office email for help with career planning and applications.

slides.title: Résumé builder: save, preview, and download
points: Enter your contact details, experience, education, and skills.
Save your résumé and reopen it to check your changes.
Preview and download a PDF for applications.
slides.narration: Open the résumé builder and enter your current contact information, work experience, education, and skills you can demonstrate. Add credentials accurately and review spelling and dates. Choose Save Resume and wait for the confirmation before leaving. Reopen the builder to check that your saved work appears. Use Preview to review the layout, then Download PDF to keep a copy for job applications. You can also upload an existing résumé from this page. Update your résumé when you gain skills or earn a credential, and ask staff for help through inter-office email.

slides.title: Credential uploads: submit and track review
points: Choose your program and the appropriate credential.
Upload a clear supported file and submit it.
Check Your submissions for review status or corrections.
slides.narration: Use Upload an earned credential for certificates, licenses, prerequisites, and exam results that you have actually earned. Choose the matching enrolled program and credential when available. Upload a readable PDF or supported image and submit it. Check Your submissions to see the file and its review status. Submitted for review means the file is waiting for staff verification; it does not mean approved. If a submission is rejected, read the reason and provide corrected evidence. Keep your original credential. Contact staff through inter-office email if your program or credential is missing from the choices.

hvac.title: Your six-week HVAC training journey
hvac.subtitle: Four weeks of self-paced study. Two weeks of scheduled hands-on training.

slides.title: Six weeks: online study, then hands-on
points: Weeks 1–4: self-paced online learning
Weeks 5–6: scheduled hands-on training
Confirm your individual dates with David

The next two weeks focus on scheduled hands-on training. Self-paced does not mean unscheduled: follow the deadlines and course sequence in your assigned plan. Your enrollment dates and David’s confirmed training appointment control when and where you attend. Do not arrive at a facility without a confirmed appointment.

Report missing access or a blocked lesson promptly so your practical training is not delayed.

slides.title: Contact David to schedule practical training
points: David Nazaire
indyondemandservices@gmail.com
slides.narration: Contact David Nazaire to arrange the hands-on portion of your HVAC program. His saved program contact number is two one five, two one four, nine three five five. His email is indyondemandservices at gmail dot com. Tell him your full name, that you are an Elevate HVAC learner, your online-study progress, and the dates you are available. Ask him to confirm the training dates, times, location, required clothing, tools, and safety equipment. Wait for confirmation before attending.

slides.title: Before your hands-on appointment
points: Finish the assigned online prerequisites
Confirm the location and safety requirements
Bring the materials David specifies
slides.narration: Before hands-on training, complete the online work David or your syllabus requires. Review safety lessons and write down the questions you want to practice. Confirm the appointment, travel plans, arrival time, clothing, tools, and personal protective equipment with David. Do not guess which equipment to bring. At the facility, follow the instructor’s directions and record attendance through the assigned process. Hands-on competency requires supervised performance and instructor verification; watching an example does not certify a practical skill.

apprentice.title: Build your skills, one training day at a time
apprentice.subtitle: Connect your theory lessons, shop practice, hours, and supervisor feedback.

slides.title: Two connected parts of apprenticeship
points: RTI: related theory instruction
OJL: supervised training at your approved shop
Each has its own evidence and progress
slides.narration: Your apprenticeship combines related technical instruction, or RTI, with supervised on-the-job learning, or OJL. Use the assigned course for theory, examples, and knowledge checks. Your approved shop and qualified supervisor provide practical training. Pictures and videos explain procedures, but they do not replace supervised practice or a competency sign-off. Read your own registered program plan and syllabus so you understand the hours, competencies, and evidence that apply to your occupation.

slides.title: Your daily apprentice routine
points: Read your next RTI lesson
Clock in at your approved worksite
Check hours and supervisor feedback
slides.narration: Open your apprentice dashboard each training day. Review announcements and your next theory lesson. At the approved shop, allow the location permissions the timeclock needs and clock in before supervised work starts. Record only the actual activity and time you completed. Clock out before you leave. Do not overlap theory study and supervised work entries. If a location or timeclock error occurs, tell your supervisor and request a correction with accurate dates, times, and evidence.

slides.title: Skill practice and verification
points: Practice with your assigned supervisor
Request sign-off after demonstrating the skill
Review returned work and corrections
slides.narration: Your competency checklist shows the skills your registered apprenticeship requires. Ask your supervisor which skill you should practice next. Demonstrate it safely under the required supervision, then ask the supervisor to record the observed evidence and sign-off. A self-reported completion, printed checklist, or watched video is not a verified practical competency. Review feedback and repeat practice when needed. Use the dashboard to check which records are submitted, approved, or returned for correction.

slides.title: Your weekly review
points: Review approved and pending hours
Check RTI lessons and quizzes
Plan the next week with your supervisor
slides.narration: Before the week ends, compare your clock entries, approved training hours, theory progress, and competency checklist. Follow the limits and targets shown in your program plan; do not invent extra hours to reach a target. Ask about a pending or returned entry before it becomes a reporting problem. Check your schedule and agree on the next week’s practical training with your shop supervisor. Contact Elevate if you cannot reach your shop or the assigned course is unavailable.

slides.title: Documents, payments, and support
points: Read your actual agreement
Use protected uploads and official invoices
Ask staff about a hold or incorrect balance
slides.narration: Keep required agreements, documents, and contact information current. Review any invoice or payment-plan terms in your own account. A displayed amount or due date should match your signed agreement; report a mismatch rather than paying an unfamiliar request. Do not send card details or identity documents through chat. A document submission may still need staff review. Use the dashboard support and communication tools to report an access hold, disputed hour, safety concern, or schedule problem.

host-shop.title: Help your apprentices grow with confidence
host-shop.subtitle: Plan supervision, verify training, and keep your shop records together.

slides.title: Welcome to your Host Shop workspace
points: Your shop, apprentices, and supervisor
Training evidence in one place
One clear next action at a time
slides.narration: Your Host Shop dashboard is the working record for your approved apprenticeship site. Confirm your shop name, assigned apprentices, and supervisor. Review the next required actions first. An assigned apprentice still needs the correct registered program, schedule, supervision, and documentation. Use the dashboard to coordinate training, review actual hours, record competency evidence, and communicate with Elevate. If the wrong apprentice or shop appears, stop and ask Administration to correct the assignment.

slides.title: Plan safe supervised training
points: Review the registered work process
Assign a qualified supervisor
Match practical work to the apprentice’s progress
slides.narration: Open the apprentice’s assigned program and review the work process, supervision requirements, and current progress. Plan safe practical work that fits the apprentice’s training stage. Confirm who will supervise the session and what tools and supplies are needed. Explain the task, observe performance, and give feedback. Theory coursework and shop practice are connected, but one does not replace the other. Report an unsafe task, missing supervisor, or incorrect program assignment before training continues.

slides.title: Review hours and location exceptions
points: Approve actual supervised time
Return incorrect entries with a reason
Never manufacture or duplicate hours
slides.narration: Review each apprentice’s time entries against the work you supervised. Confirm dates, start and finish times, breaks, activity, and supporting evidence. Approve accurate entries and return incorrect entries with a clear correction note. A geofence exception is a reason to investigate; it is not proof that all claimed time was supervised. Ask for the actual facts and use the correction process. Do not estimate, duplicate, or approve hours you cannot support.

slides.title: Record competency sign-offs
points: Select the correct apprentice and skill
Observe the required performance
Save the evidence and verification
slides.narration: Open Competencies and select the assigned apprentice and registered skill. Observe the required performance and record the date, task, outcome, and supporting evidence. Sign only after the apprentice has demonstrated the skill at the required standard. If more practice is needed, record useful feedback and the next practice step. A printed checklist, watched video, or student request alone is not a completed electronic verification. Confirm the saved sign-off appears in the record.

slides.title: Keep shop documents and agreements current
points: Read your assigned MOU
Upload requested licenses and insurance
Respond to correction or expiry notices
slides.narration: Open Documents and Guides and Agreements. Read the agreement assigned to your shop and the responsibilities it creates. Upload only the requested current records, such as applicable licenses, insurance, and supervisor evidence. Check whether each submission is pending review, approved, or returned. Replace an expired or rejected item with the correct file and explanation. Uploading a document does not certify its authenticity or automatically approve the shop. Ask Administration about a requirement that does not fit your occupation.

slides.title: Communicate, report, and close the week
points: Check shop messages and meetings
Resolve missing evidence before deadlines
Report safety and attendance concerns
slides.narration: Use the shop’s dashboard communication tools for apprentice and Elevate coordination. Check announcements, messages, and confirmed appointments. Keep a written next action and follow-up date when a learner is absent or struggling. Before a reporting deadline, review attendance, RTI, OJL, wages, competencies, and exceptions. Report safety incidents or supervision problems promptly. Closeout requires the applicable verified records; do not mark a learner complete just because the scheduled training period ended.

program-holder.title: A clear path for every learner you support
program-holder.subtitle: From first contact to verified completion: your daily operations guide.

slides.title: Start with your assigned programs
points: Confirm your organization and role
Review applicants and active learners
Open the next required action
slides.narration: Your Program Holder dashboard connects applicants, students, training, records, communication, and payment readiness. Confirm your organization, assigned programs, and contact details. Review the next required action and any at-risk learners before starting new work. Applicants are not the same as enrolled students. Open the appropriate record, check its status, and identify who owns the next action. Report an incorrect program, learner, mailbox, or organization before accessing or changing records.

slides.title: Contact applicants and document outcomes
points: Review the application and program
Call or email through your assigned office tools
Save the outcome and follow-up date
slides.narration: Open Applicants and review the applicant’s program interest and current next step. Contact the person through your assigned office phone or email. Confirm their interest, explain the next action, and record the outcome in the account. When funding applies, direct the applicant through the required agency process and document the result. Do not promise a voucher, eligibility decision, job, or payment. End each contact with a clear action, responsible person, and follow-up date.

slides.title: Explain how each assigned course works
points: Read the actual syllabus and schedule
Explain online and practical requirements separately
Confirm the first assignment and instructor contact
slides.narration: Open Programs and the assigned syllabus before explaining a course. Confirm the duration, learning provider, required lessons, quizzes, assignments, practical training, credential, and completion evidence. Do not use one program’s hours or schedule for another program. Give each enrolled learner a clear first assignment and a way to contact the instructor. If the program includes hands-on training, confirm the location, supervisor, schedule, and prerequisites. Report missing course access before the learner falls behind.

slides.title: Manage enrolled and at-risk learners
points: Check progress and missed assignments
Contact the learner before the deadline
Record the barrier and intervention
slides.narration: Open Students to review confirmed enrollments and active training. Check attendance, lesson and assignment progress, upcoming deadlines, and instructor feedback. Use the at-risk view to focus follow-up. Ask what the learner is working on, what is incomplete, and what is blocking progress. Give a specific next action and due date and record the response. Escalate unresolved access, funding, safety, instructor, or worksite problems rather than leaving the account idle.

slides.title: Clear documents and required agreements
points: Upload registration, insurance, W-9, and credentials as requested
Read the handbook and assigned agreements
Separate your tasks from Elevate review
slides.narration: Open Documents and Compliance. Review each applicable item and identify whether you, Elevate, or both parties own the next step. Upload the requested current records through the protected form. Pending review means the file is submitted and awaits review; do not repeatedly upload it. Read rejection or correction notes before replacing a document. Review and sign only the agreement assigned to your organization, including scope, privacy, payment terms, responsibilities, and termination provisions.

slides.title: Record hours, skills, and completion evidence
points: Use actual dates and supervised activities
Verify the program’s own completion requirements
Finish closeout before requesting a payout
slides.narration: Record actual training and supervised activity with dates, hours, outcomes, and supporting evidence. Never duplicate, estimate, or backdate records. Before marking a learner complete, verify the required coursework, assessments, hours, practical skills where applicable, credentials, and final records. Submit the reporting period and resolve missing evidence. Payout readiness follows the signed agreement, verified milestones, compliance, and receipt of applicable funding. A lead, phone call, or attendance claim alone does not create a payment.

slides.title: Your daily office routine
points: Check phone, Inbox, and appointments
Document every follow-up in the account
Use PARIS for guidance; verify facts yourself
slides.narration: Check your assigned phone connection, Inbox, calendar, and required actions each working day. Use the correct From address and extension when contacting applicants or learners. Keep program communication in the official workspace so the record stays connected. For a meeting, confirm the appointment and join link and test your chosen microphone or camera before it starts. PARIS can help explain a page or prepare a draft; review facts and recipients before sending or submitting anything.

slides.title: Check student dates against the source record
points: Open Students and find the learner
Compare start, scheduled end and actual completion
Report a mismatch with the uploaded source
slides.narration: Open Students, find the learner by name, and compare the recorded training dates with the uploaded voucher or approved schedule. A voucher service window can differ from the actual training or completion date. Do not use the voucher expiration date as a completion date. Do not mark a learner complete to remove an overdue alert. Send Administration the learner name, field, source document and requested correction. Missing dates remain missing until the evidence is checked.

slides.title: Email a student from your assigned roster
points: Open Email → Compose
Choose a student or office contact
Review To, subject and message before Send
slides.narration: Open Email and confirm that the From address is your assigned Elevate mailbox. Select Compose, then Choose a student or office contact. Your assigned students appear automatically when their email is recorded and contact access is authorized. Selecting a contact adds the address to To; confirm every recipient before writing or sending. Missing contacts require a record correction, not an invented email address. Read replies in the same conversation. A provider accepting an email does not guarantee delivery or that the student read it.

slides.title: Record training and verify the saved result
points: Open Hours and choose the correct student
Enter actual dates, activities and hours
Submit and check the review status
slides.narration: Open Hours and select the assigned student and program. Enter the actual training date, hours, work completed and supporting details. Review before submitting and confirm the saved entry appears. Submitted records may still require verification. Do not copy another student’s hours or treat an empty history as proof that training did not occur. Report missing or incorrect entries with the actual date and supporting evidence.

slides.title: Complete the weekly student progress report
points: Open Reports and choose the student
Record progress, barriers and supporting evidence
Review and submit; check it appears in history
slides.narration: Open Reports and choose an active student. Record this week’s lessons, skills practiced, attendance, hours, assignments, scores, barriers, contact and next-week goals using the evidence available. Do not enter an assessment result that has not been earned. Review the full report, submit it, and confirm it appears in submitted reports. Complete one report for each active student each Friday. PARIS can help prepare a draft; the Program Holder remains responsible for verifying the record.

slides.title: Plan meetings and follow-ups
points: Open Calendar and meetings
Check the date, time and attendee
Save the meeting and confirm the details
slides.narration: Use Calendar and meetings for scheduled advising, progress checks and training meetings. Confirm the time zone, date, attendee and meeting link. Check the saved record before telling the student the meeting is confirmed. Keep the next follow-up with the student’s notes so another authorized team member can understand what happens next. If you need to reschedule, update the saved meeting and notify the attendee so that both calendars agree.

slides.title: Connect students with career and community support
points: Open Career services or Community
Show students where to find opportunities
Use their learner account for personal submissions
slides.narration: Show students their Career services area for opportunities and coaching, and explain how their own resume and credential tools support placement. Do not submit a resume or credential on a student’s behalf without the appropriate authority. Use Community for professional introductions, questions and portfolio work. Protect personal documents, grades, vouchers and funding information; those belong in protected records, not public posts.

site-coordinator.title: Bring your regional training team together
site-coordinator.subtitle: Coordinate people, programs, sites, and follow-up with a clear next action.

slides.title: Your regional coordination role
points: Confirm your assigned region and organizations
Keep program delivery and records connected
Escalate decisions outside your authority
slides.narration: Your Site Coordinator dashboard connects regional intake, Program Holders, host sites, active learners, reporting, and follow-up. Confirm the regional assignment and responsibilities in your own signed agreement. Use only the organizations, programs, and records assigned to you. A coordinator organizes and documents the next step; the role does not automatically authorize every funding, eligibility, access, or credential decision. Route those decisions to the responsible authorized staff and record the outcome.

slides.title: Move regional applicants to a clear next step
points: Review applicant interest and location
Confirm the assigned program and contact
Record the action, owner, and due date
slides.narration: Review newly routed applicants for your region. Confirm their program interest, location, and correct program contact. Explain the current application, onboarding, and agency steps without promising approval. Assign or coordinate follow-up using the tools available to your role. Keep a contact outcome and next action on every active account. If a program has no assigned qualified Program Holder, coordinate with Elevate to resolve the gap rather than telling the applicant that training is ready when it is not.

slides.title: Support Program Holders and host sites
points: Confirm the qualified training contact
Check agreement and document readiness
Resolve supervision and scheduling gaps
slides.narration: Coordinate with approved Program Holders and host shops for the programs assigned to your region. Confirm who teaches the theory, who supervises practical training, and where learners attend. Review operational readiness, agreements, document issues, and missing assignments through authorized records. Do not invent an instructor, location, start date, or approval. Escalate a missing qualified provider or unsafe site before learners are scheduled to attend. Record who is responsible for closing each gap.

slides.title: Monitor learning and intervene early
points: Review attendance, progress, and barriers
Check practical training arrangements
Track the follow-up until resolved
slides.narration: Review active learners and any at-risk flags regularly. Confirm that course links, the first assignment, and the program contact are available. Where practical training is required, confirm the scheduled site and supervisor. Follow up on absence, stalled progress, missing paperwork, and learner support needs. Document the learner’s response, the action taken, and the next review date. Share only the information needed with authorized staff and the assigned provider.

slides.title: Report verified regional outcomes
points: Reconcile hours and completion evidence
Keep funding decisions with the authorized agency
Submit accurate reports and closeout
slides.narration: Before submitting regional reports, reconcile the applicable enrollment, attendance, training, credential, placement, and closeout records. Do not report an unsupported outcome or assume that a provider’s message is verified evidence. WorkOne and other responsible agencies determine their funding decisions; record written outcomes through the approved workflow. Follow your signed regional agreement for reporting and compensation. Escalate missing evidence and unresolved account conflicts before marking a reporting period complete.

slides.title: Clear documents and required agreements
points: Upload registration, insurance, W-9, and credentials as requested
Read the handbook and assigned agreements
Separate your tasks from Elevate review
slides.narration: Open Documents and Compliance. Review each applicable item and identify whether you, Elevate, or both parties own the next step. Upload the requested current records through the protected form. Pending review means the file is submitted and awaits review; do not repeatedly upload it. Read rejection or correction notes before replacing a document. Review and sign only the agreement assigned to your organization, including scope, privacy, payment terms, responsibilities, and termination provisions.
